title: Cultivar, Strain, Line, Accession, and Clone
objective: Use plant-genetic-resource terms precisely and attach each name to a reproducible biological unit.

terms.definition: A cultivated plant grouping defined by reproducible distinguishing characteristics under an applicable system.
Informal cannabis market term whose genetic, legal, and taxonomic meaning is often unspecified.
Breeding population or family maintained through a defined mating and selection history.
Distinct sample maintained in a germplasm collection with a unique identifier and provenance.

coreScience: These words describe different kinds of identity. A cultivar or protected variety is a plant grouping, not merely a memorable name. A line is defined by breeding history and may still segregate. An accession is a conserved sample and documentation unit. A clone is a vegetatively propagated ramet derived from one source genotype.

In cannabis commerce, strain often labels a product or claimed lineage without an enforceable identity standard. Samples sold under one name have shown substantial genetic differences, while differently named samples can be close. The word can be retained for audience recognition, but it must not replace source, generation, clone code, or test data.

Seed lots from one named cultivar are not equivalent to a single clone. A clone name should refer to a documented source plant or reference sample. A line name should include generation, family, and selection history. An accession identifier must remain tied to the conserving institution and acquisition record.
cultivationRelevance: Use a layered identity string: displayed name; breeder or repository; cultivar, line, accession, or clone status; generation or seed lot; internal plant ID; and verified genotype or chemotype records.
Never rename material to match appearance or aroma. Quarantine unknowns under a temporary code until provenance and tests support a controlled designation.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Exact spelling, breeder or source, date received, and claims supplied.
Clone, seed lot, family, line, accession, population, or unknown.
Parent IDs, generation, lot, mother source, number of passages, and dates.
Reference sample, genotype panel, chemistry, morphology, photographs, and certificates.
Old name, new controlled name, authority, reason, date, and affected inventory.

misconceptions: A strain name is a genotype: The same market name can contain genetically divergent material.
A seed cultivar is a clone: Seed reproduction creates segregating individuals unless the material is exceptionally uniform.
An accession is a cultivar: An accession may represent a cultivar, line, landrace, wild population, or other conserved sample.
evidenceLimits: Legal definitions of cultivar or variety vary by jurisdiction and protection system. Genetic similarity alone does not establish ownership, distinctness, uniformity, stability, or right to use a name.
